original_question: Let A and B be generators of C0 -semigroups on a Banach space X. (i) Define the sum C = A + B such that C becomes a (maximal) closed operator on X and Cx = Ãx + B̃x for all x ∈ X and some extrapolated operators A and B. (ii) Find assumptions on A and B such that C remains a generator on X, thereby unifying known perturbation results.
target_in_paper: Section 1, Problem 7 (“A+B problem”) in the generation-problems section. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))
correct_elements: Your draft already reproduces almost verbatim the official two-part open problem: A and B are generators of C0-semigroups on a Banach space X; one asks first for a definition of C = A + B as a (maximal) closed operator on X via suitable extrapolated operators, and then for hypotheses ensuring that C is again a generator on X, with the aim of unifying perturbation results. missing_details: Add the exact label used in the paper: this is Problem 7, the “A+B problem,” in Section 1 (“Generation problems”). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))
State explicitly that the paper asks for C to be a “(maximal) closed operator” on X, not merely a formal or closable sum. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))

Use the paper’s formulation Cx = \widetilde{A}x + \widetilde{B}x for all x ∈ X, with suitable extrapolated operators of A and B; the paper does not specify a particular extrapolation-space formalism, so a faithful rewrite should not impose one. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))

Include the concrete test case supplied in the nearby comment: X = C0(ℝ,E) or X = L^p(ℝ,E), Af = f′, and (Bf)(s) = C(s)f(s) for appropriate f and closed operators C(s) on E. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))

Do not add extra standing assumptions not present in the paper (such as commutativity, analyticity, sectoriality, or a specified scalar field); the whole point is to discover hypotheses under which the sum generates. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))
refined_question: Given generators A and B of C0-semigroups on a Banach space X, can one define a sum C = A + B in such a way that C is a (maximal) closed operator on X and satisfies Cx = \widetilde{A}x + \widetilde{B}x for every x ∈ X for suitable extrapolated operators \widetilde{A} and \widetilde{B} of A and B, and can one then identify hypotheses on A and B ensuring that this operator C again generates a C0-semigroup on X, in a form that unifies the known perturbation results? As a basic test case, treat X = C0(ℝ,E) or X = L^p(ℝ,E), with Af = f′ and (Bf)(s) = C(s)f(s) for appropriate f and closed operators C(s) on E. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2410.00416))

The abstract confirms that arXiv:2410.00416 is a curated list of unsolved open problems, so the faithful target here is the open problem itself, not a neighboring theorem or a broader perturbation program. The only substantial nearby context that should be folded into a stand-alone formulation is the comment giving the standard test case on C0(ℝ,E) or L^p(ℝ,E).
